editorial:
You wake up in a locked room with no explanation, and fifteen years later you are suddenly free with nothing but rage and questions. That is the wild ride Oldboy takes you on, following Oh Dae-su as he tries to find who stole his life and why. It is dark, intense, and strange, but it pulls you in with a mystery that keeps getting bigger. The movie mixes revenge, romance, and shocking secrets, so you never feel safe guessing what comes next.

The acting is strong, especially Choi Min-sik as Dae-su, who makes every punch, scream, and quiet moment feel real. The hallway fight is famous for a reason, and the pacing keeps the story moving even when it gets heavy. It is violent and disturbing, so it is not for everyone, and some twists may feel too much. If you like bold thrillers and can handle dark themes, this is a must-see.
endingExplained: In the end, Dae-su learns his captor, Lee Woo-jin, punished him because Dae-su once saw Woo-jin with his sister, leading to her death. The bigger shock is that Mi-do, the woman Dae-su loves, is actually his daughter. To punish himself, Dae-su cuts out his tongue and asks a hypnotist to erase his memory. The final scene shows him smiling, leaving you unsure if the trick worked or if he still remembers everything.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark revenge thrillers with shocking twists.
